name: Acajou Red
lede: Acajou Red is a grayish red from Ridgway's 1912 plates, filed by the ISCC-NBS system in 1955, and measured in our color graph as nearly identical to a different Wikipedia-sourced name, Middle Red Purple.

sections.title: Two catalogues, one near-identical red
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* places this hue at plate XIII, hue 1′, tone i, scanned from an aged plate and so approximate [1]. The ISCC-NBS system later filed it as a moderate red [1]. Our library notes that a separately sourced name, Middle Red Purple, measures only 0.9 units away, close enough to call the two the same color under different catalogues [2].

Its closest named relatives in our color graph are [[english-red]] and [[pompeian-red]], both more vivid and within 3.6 units [3].

Further out are [[redwood]], almost the same at 3.6 units, and [[reddish-chestnut]], also almost the same [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, a color within six units of Acajou Red covers at least five per cent of a canvas in 148 works, with the 1400s carrying it at nearly four times the archive's overall rate [4]. It is strikingly linked to Kalighat painting, at nearly 42 times the expected rate, and to works from India and Tibet generally [4]. A 1720 Rasikapriya page carries it across more than 40 per cent of the canvas [4]. It most often shares a canvas with brick and terracotta [4]. These remain photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors [4].

questions.q: Which separately named color is a near-exact match for Acajou Red?
True or false: Acajou Red is strongly overrepresented in Kalighat painting from Bengal.

openers: Acajou Red is just 0.9 units from a different catalogue's Middle Red Purple, essentially the same color twice.

issues: No source in our records documents the choice of the name "Acajou" beyond the catalogue entries.
